paragraphs.text: Κατ’ ἐκεῖνον δὲ τὸν καιρὸν ἐπέβαλεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ βασιλεὺς τὰς χεῖρας κακῶσαί τινας τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας.
paragraphs.translit: Kat’ ekeinon de ton kairon epebalen Hērōdēs ho basileus tas cheiras kakōsai tinas tōn apo tēs ekklēsias.

i18n.en: Now about that time, Herod the king laid hands on some of those from the church to harm them.

paragraphs.text: ἀνεῖλεν δὲ Ἰάκωβον τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰωάννου μαχαίρῃ.
paragraphs.translit: aneilen de Iakōbon ton adelphon Iōannou machairē.

i18n.en: And he killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.

paragraphs.commentary: Herod Agrippa I (the grandson of Herod the Great, king of Judea 41-44 CE) executes James the brother of John — the first apostolic martyrdom recorded in Acts. The historical-political context is Herod Agrippa I's persecution of the early-Jerusalem-Christian-community c. 41-44 CE. See central-glossary entry `peter-prison-release-acts-12-daniel-6-angelic-deliverance-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὅτι ἀρεστόν ἐστιν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις προσέθετο συλλαβεῖν καὶ Πέτρον (ἦσαν δὲ ἡμέραι τῶν ἀζύμων),
paragraphs.translit: idōn de hoti areston estin tois Ioudaiois prosetheto syllabein kai Petron (ēsan de hai hēmerai tōn azymōn),

i18n.en: And when he saw that it was pleasing to the Jews, he proceeded to arrest Peter also (these were the days of Unleavened Bread),

paragraphs.text: ὃν καὶ πιάσας ἔθετο εἰς φυλακήν, παραδοὺς τέσσαρσιν τετραδίοις στρατιωτῶν φυλάσσειν αὐτόν, βουλόμενος μετὰ τὸ πάσχα ἀναγαγεῖν αὐτὸν τῷ λαῷ.
paragraphs.translit: hon kai piasas etheto eis phylakēn, paradous tessarsin tetradiois stratiōtōn phylassein auton, boulomenos meta to pascha anagagein auton tō laō.

i18n.en: and when he had seized him, he put him in prison, delivering him over to four squads of soldiers to guard him, intending to bring him out to the people after the Passover.

paragraphs.commentary: *tetradiois stratiōtōn* 'four squads of four soldiers' — the heavy guard emphasizes the deliverance as more-clearly-miraculous.

paragraphs.text: ὁ μὲν οὖν Πέτρος ἐτηρεῖτο ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ· προσευχὴ δὲ ἦν ἐκτενῶς γινομένη ὑπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας πρὸς τὸν θεὸν περὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho men oun Petros etēreito en tē phylakē· proseuchē de ēn ektenōs ginomenē hypo tēs ekklēsias pros ton theon peri autou.

i18n.en: So Peter was kept in prison; but earnest prayer for him was being made to God by the church.

paragraphs.text: Ὅτε δὲ ἤμελλεν προαγαγεῖν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἡρῴδης, τῇ νυκτὶ ἐκείνῃ ἦν ὁ Πέτρος κοιμώμενος μεταξὺ δύο στρατιωτῶν δεδεμένος ἁλύσεσιν δυσίν, φύλακές τε πρὸ τῆς θύρας ἐτήρουν τὴν φυλακήν.
paragraphs.translit: Hote de ēmellen proagagein auton ho Hērōdēs, tē nykti ekeinē ēn ho Petros koimōmenos metaxy dyo stratiōtōn dedemenos halysesin dysin, phylakes te pro tēs thyras etēroun tēn phylakēn.

i18n.en: And when Herod was about to bring him out, that very night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards before the door were keeping the prison.

paragraphs.commentary: **MAJOR ANGELIC-DELIVERANCE NARRATIVE.** Cross-corpus to Dan 3 (fiery-furnace-rescue) + Dan 6 (lion's-den-rescue) + Acts 5:17-26 (first apostolic prison-release). Characteristic features of the Lukan-Acts angelic-deliverance pattern: night-time setting + bright-light appearance + chains-falling-off + prison-gates opening of their own accord + iron-gate opening of its own accord. Documented at the central-glossary entry `peter-prison-release-acts-12-daniel-6-angelic-deliverance-cross-corpus`. The Raëlian-canon engagement (Raël 1975) is acknowledged-without-endorsement per the established framework.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου ἐπέστη, καὶ φῶς ἔλαμψεν ἐν τῷ οἰκήματι· πατάξας δὲ τὴν πλευρὰν τοῦ Πέτρου ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Ἀνάστα ἐν τάχει· καὶ ἐξέπεσαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἁλύσεις ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai idou angelos kyriou epestē, kai phōs elampsen en tō oikēmati· pataxas de tēn pleuran tou Petrou ēgeiren auton legōn· Anasta en tachei· kai exepesan autou hai halyseis ek tōn cheirōn.

i18n.en: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the cell. And striking Peter on the side, he woke him, saying: "Get up quickly." And the chains fell off his hands.

paragraphs.commentary: *kai idou angelos kyriou epestē ... kai exepesan autou hai halyseis ek tōn cheirōn* 'and behold, the angel of the Lord stood-beside-him ... and his chains fell off from his hands'. The *epestē* angelic-appearance verb is paralleled by *exaposteilas ho kyrios ton angelon autou* 'the Lord sent his angel' at v.11 (Peter's recognition-confession after the deliverance). The doubled-verb pattern is characteristic of Lukan-Acts angelic-deliverance narratives.

paragraphs.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος πρὸς αὐτόν· Ζῶσαι καὶ ὑπόδησαι τὰ σανδάλιά σου· ἐποίησεν δὲ οὕτως. καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Περιβαλοῦ τὸ ἱμάτιόν σου καὶ ἀκολούθει μοι·
paragraphs.translit: eipen de ho angelos pros auton· Zōsai kai hypodēsai ta sandalia sou· epoiēsen de houtōs. kai legei autō· Peribalou to himation sou kai akolouthei moi·

i18n.en: And the angel said to him: "Gird yourself and put on your sandals." And he did so. And he says to him: "Throw your cloak around you and follow me."

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἠκολούθει, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει ὅτι ἀληθές ἐστιν τὸ γινόμενον διὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου, ἐδόκει δὲ ὅραμα βλέπειν.
paragraphs.translit: kai exelthōn ēkolouthei, kai ouk ēdei hoti alēthes estin to ginomenon dia tou angelou, edokei de horama blepein.

i18n.en: And going out, he followed, and did not know that what was happening through the angel was real, but thought he was seeing a vision.

paragraphs.text: διελθόντες δὲ πρώτην φυλακὴν καὶ δευτέραν ἦλθαν ἐπὶ τὴν πύλην τὴν σιδηρᾶν τὴν φέρουσαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, ἥτις αὐτομάτη ἠνοίγη αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐξελθόντες προῆλθον ῥύμην μίαν, καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέστη ὁ ἄγγελος ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: dielthontes de prōtēn phylakēn kai deuteran ēlthan epi tēn pylēn tēn sidēran tēn pherousan eis tēn polin, hētis automatē ēnoigē autois, kai exelthontes proēlthon rhymēn mian, kai eutheōs apestē ho angelos ap’ autou.

i18n.en: And having passed the first guard-post and the second, they came to the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened to them of its own accord; and going out, they went down one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὁ Πέτρος ἐν ἑαυτῷ γενόμενος εἶπεν· Νῦν οἶδα ἀληθῶς ὅτι ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ κύριος τὸν ἄγγελον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξείλατό με ἐκ χειρὸς Ἡρῴδου καὶ πάσης τῆς προσδοκίας τοῦ λαοῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho Petros en heautō genomenos eipen· Nyn oida alēthōs hoti exapesteilen ho kyrios ton angelon autou kai exeilato me ek cheiros Hērōdou kai pasēs tēs prosdokias tou laou tōn Ioudaiōn.

i18n.en: And when Peter came to himself, he said: "Now I know truly that the Lord has sent his angel and rescued me from the hand of Herod and from all the expectation of the Jewish people."

paragraphs.text: συνιδών τε ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν τῆς Μαρίας τῆς μητρὸς Ἰωάννου τοῦ ἐπικαλουμένου Μάρκου, οὗ ἦσαν ἱκανοὶ συνηθροισμένοι καὶ προσευχόμενοι.
paragraphs.translit: synidōn te ēlthen epi tēn oikian tēs Marias tēs mētros Iōannou tou epikaloumenou Markou, hou ēsan hikanoi synēthroismenoi kai proseuchomenoi.

i18n.en: And when he had considered this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark, where many were gathered together and praying.

paragraphs.text: κρούσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ τὴν θύραν τοῦ πυλῶνος προσῆλθε παιδίσκη ὑπακοῦσαι ὀνόματι Ῥόδη,
paragraphs.translit: krousantos de autou tēn thyran tou pylōnos prosēlthe paidiskē hypakousai onomati Rhodē,

i18n.en: And when he knocked at the door of the gateway, a maidservant named Rhoda came to answer.

paragraphs.commentary: The Rhoda-narrative (vv.13-16) — Lukan-Acts narrative integrates humor into the deliverance-pattern: Rhoda hears Peter's voice at the gate but in her excitement leaves him knocking outside; the community doubts her ('You are out of your mind' v.15); they finally open the gate. The comic-narrative element distinguishes Acts 12 from the more-solemn Daniel-tradition.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ Πέτρου ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς οὐκ ἤνοιξεν τὸν πυλῶνα, εἰσδραμοῦσα δὲ ἀπήγγειλεν ἑστάναι τὸν Πέτρον πρὸ τοῦ πυλῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: kai epignousa tēn phōnēn tou Petrou apo tēs charas ouk ēnoixen ton pylōna, eisdramousa de apēngeilen hestanai ton Petron pro tou pylōnos.

i18n.en: And recognizing Peter's voice, in her joy she did not open the gate, but ran in and announced that Peter was standing before the gate.

paragraphs.text: οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπαν· Μαίνῃ. ἡ δὲ διϊσχυρίζετο οὕτως ἔχειν. οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον· Ὁ ἄγγελός ἐστιν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de pros autēn eipan· Mainē. hē de diischyrizeto houtōs echein. hoi de elegon· Ho angelos estin autou.

i18n.en: But they said to her: "You are out of your mind." But she kept insisting that it was so. And they said: "It is his angel."

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἐπέμενεν κρούων· ἀνοίξαντες δὲ εἶδαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐξέστησαν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Petros epemenen krouōn· anoixantes de eidan auton kai exestēsan.

i18n.en: But Peter kept on knocking; and when they had opened, they saw him and were amazed.

paragraphs.text: κατασείσας δὲ αὐτοῖς τῇ χειρὶ σιγᾶν διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ὁ κύριος αὐτὸν ἐξήγαγεν ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς, εἶπέν τε· Ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰακώβῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ταῦτα. καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη εἰς ἕτερον τόπον.
paragraphs.translit: kataseisas de autois tē cheiri sigan diēgēsato autois pōs ho kyrios auton exēgagen ek tēs phylakēs, eipen te· Apangeilate Iakōbō kai tois adelphois tauta. kai exelthōn eporeuthē eis heteron topon.

i18n.en: Motioning to them with his hand to be silent, he described to them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison, and said: "Report these things to James and to the brothers." And he departed and went to another place.

paragraphs.text: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ἦν τάραχος οὐκ ὀλίγος ἐν τοῖς στρατιώταις, τί ἄρα ὁ Πέτρος ἐγένετο.
paragraphs.translit: Genomenēs de hēmeras ēn tarachos ouk oligos en tois stratiōtais, ti ara ho Petros egeneto.

i18n.en: Now when day came, there was no small commotion among the soldiers as to what had become of Peter.

paragraphs.text: Ἡρῴδης δὲ ἐπιζητήσας αὐτὸν καὶ μὴ εὑρὼν ἀνακρίνας τοὺς φύλακας ἐκέλευσεν ἀπαχθῆναι, καὶ κατελθὼν ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς Καισάρειαν διέτριβεν.
paragraphs.translit: Hērōdēs de epizētēsas auton kai mē heurōn anakrinas tous phylakas ekeleusen apachthēnai, kai katelthōn apo tēs Ioudaias eis Kaisareian dietriben.

i18n.en: And when Herod had searched for him and not found him, he examined the guards and commanded that they be led away; and he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.

paragraphs.text: Ἦν δὲ θυμομαχῶν Τυρίοις καὶ Σιδωνίοις· ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ παρῆσαν πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ πείσαντες Βλάστον τὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ κοιτῶνος τοῦ βασιλέως ᾐτοῦντο εἰρήνην διὰ τὸ τρέφεσθαι αὐτῶν τὴν χώραν ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλικῆς.
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de thymomachōn Tyriois kai Sidōniois· homothymadon de parēsan pros auton, kai peisantes Blaston ton epi tou koitōnos tou basileōs ētounto eirēnēn dia to trephesthai autōn tēn chōran apo tēs basilikēs.

i18n.en: Now he was at fierce odds with the Tyrians and the Sidonians; and with one accord they came to him, and having persuaded Blastus the king's chamberlain, they sought peace, because their country was fed from the king's country.

paragraphs.text: τακτῇ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἐνδυσάμενος ἐσθῆτα βασιλικὴν καὶ καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐδημηγόρει πρὸς αὐτούς·
paragraphs.translit: taktē de hēmera ho Hērōdēs endysamenos esthēta basilikēn kai kathisas epi tou bēmatos edēmēgorei pros autous·

i18n.en: And on an appointed day, Herod, having put on royal apparel and seated on the throne, delivered an oration to them.

paragraphs.commentary: Herod Agrippa I's death at Caesarea (vv.21-23). Cross-corpus to Josephus Antiquities 19.343-350 — Josephus preserves a parallel account of Agrippa's death at Caesarea with naturalistic-medical-context details (5-day illness following the festival speech). The Lukan-Acts account emphasizes the angelic-judgment for accepting divine-acclamation ('the voice of a god, not of a man' v.22); both narratives converge on the historical-event of Agrippa's sudden death in c. 44 CE. See central-glossary entry `peter-prison-release-acts-12-daniel-6-angelic-deliverance-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ δῆμος ἐπεφώνει· Θεοῦ φωνὴ καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώπου.
paragraphs.translit: ho de dēmos epephōnei· Theou phōnē kai ouk anthrōpou.

i18n.en: And the people kept shouting: "The voice of a god, and not of a man!"

paragraphs.text: παραχρῆμα δὲ ἐπάταξεν αὐτὸν ἄγγελος κυρίου ἀνθ’ ὧν οὐκ ἔδωκεν τὴν δόξαν τῷ θεῷ, καὶ γενόμενος σκωληκόβρωτος ἐξέψυξεν.
paragraphs.translit: parachrēma de epataxen auton angelos kyriou anth’ hōn ouk edōken tēn doxan tō theō, kai genomenos skōlēkobrōtos exepsyxen.

i18n.en: And immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he did not give the glory to God; and being eaten by worms, he expired.

paragraphs.text: Ὁ δὲ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐπληθύνετο.
paragraphs.translit: Ho de logos tou theou ēuxanen kai eplēthyneto.

i18n.en: But the word of God grew and multiplied.

paragraphs.text: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ καὶ Σαῦλος ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ πληρώσαντες τὴν διακονίαν, συμπαραλαβόντες Ἰωάννην τὸν ἐπικληθέντα Μάρκον.
paragraphs.translit: Barnabas de kai Saulos hypestrepsan eis Ierousalēm plērōsantes tēn diakonian, symparalabontes Iōannēn ton epiklēthenta Markon.

i18n.en: And Barnabas and Saul returned to Jerusalem when they had fulfilled their service, taking along with them John, who was called Mark.
